Quick summary of what we need to lock down to proceed with pool provisioning and SOW:
- Primary region (recommended: us-west1) and fallback region (us-central or eu-west1)
- Expected steady-state qps / concurrent requests (p95 latency targets, e.g., 200ms)
- Autoscale floor/ceiling preferences (min/max GPU nodes) and burst policy (allow burst to shared hosted capacity?)
- Compliance docs procurement asked for: SOC2 report + data-retention policy (if you can share links/attachments)

Attached: SOW_draft_v1.pdf (legal + timeline), and orion_capacity_workbook.xlsx (template for your team to fill expected traffic and model mix). Can you please:
1) Confirm primary region by EOD next Wednesday (2028-07-05)
2) Fill the workbook with expected daily QPS and peak concurrency so Rishi can size the pool
3) Indicate if procurement needs separate vendor paperwork/PO terms as early as next week

I'll loop in Engineering (Rishi) and CS (Monica) to propose a technical plan once we have the workbook back.

Thanks —

Hi Dylan —

Thanks — that outline is helpful. A few quick answers from our side:
- Primary region preference: US West (us-west1). We operate heavily on west coast customers; fallback to us-central is fine. EU is a later phase (Q4).
- Latency: aiming for p95 < 250ms for interactive flows, p95 < 500ms for batch/reranking jobs. If you can hit p95 < 200ms that’s ideal but not required for launch.
- Autoscale / burst: we are open to burst-to-shared for short spikes (less than 30 minutes) but need hard cost boundaries. Willing to set a cap on burst spend per day.

I've looped Sanjay from Ops and procurement for SOC2 and vendor paperwork. Procurement asked if you can provide a filled vendor questionnaire (I attached a link). Also, can you confirm a tentative go-live window? Our internal target is the week of 2028-07-18.

Thanks for the context — here is a proposed technical plan for Orion Health based on the workbook defaults and Claire's constraints. This is intentionally conservative for launch and can be tuned after 2 weeks in production.

1) Pool topology and region
- Primary: us-west1 (NVIDIA H100 instances, 40GB)
- Fallback: us-central1 (same instance family)
- EU: schedule in Q4 for eu-west1 when compliance + data residency are locked.

2) Model + node assumptions
- Launch model: gpt-xlarge-quant (quantized 8-bit variant) pinned for launch to keep unit costs predictable. If Orion confirms higher quality needs, we can test a 16-bit variant in canary.
- Per-node capacity estimate: ~45 concurrent small completions (or ~6 large-chat sessions) at p95 latency ~180-220ms depending on prompt lengths and batching.

3) Autoscale / burst policy (recommended)
- Min nodes: 2 (warm pool for cache/KV hotness)
- Target nodes: computed from desired concurrency; initial target = 6 nodes for steady-state traffic (fill from workbook)
- Max nodes: 20 (hard ceiling)
- Burst: allow short bursts to Hosted shared pool for up to 30 minutes, but implement daily burst spend cap of $350/day (procurement to confirm) plus realtime alert if burst spend > $150 in 15 minutes.
- Scaling cooldown: 90s for scale-up, 4m for scale-down (to avoid flapping)

4) Caching & batching configuration
- Enable prefix KV caching for chat sessions (reduces token compute)
- Aggressive dynamic batching for short requests (up to 64 tokens) with latency SLO gating

5) Observability and safety
- Provision RBAC and audit logs to Orion's SIEM ingest endpoint (link in SOW)
- Set up cost+latency dashboards in Redwood Console; enable regression alerts on prompt set (we will deploy a first eval suite).

6) Timeline (compressed to meet 2028-07-18 window)
- 2028-07-02: Redwood engineering readiness review (confirm instance type and quotas)
- 2028-07-05: Procurement & SOC2 artifacts exchanged; finalize daily burst cap
- 2028-07-09: Pool provisioned in us-west1, basic smoke tests (latency + throughput)
- 2028-07-12: Partner staging cutover, runbook validation, and security review
- 2028-07-18: Target production cutover (night window)

Attachments: redwood_capacity_plan_20280630.xlsx (includes node-sizing calc and cost estimate). Can you confirm whether Orion has fixed IP/subnet requirements for the private deployment? That will affect provisioning lead time.

If Orion confirms min/max and signs SOW by 2028-07-05 we can make the July 18 window. Otherwise expect a 2-week slip.
